What readability defects exist per skill, with quoted passages?

keyFindings.text: **Readability: routing precedes instructions and jargon precedes definition.** In `sk-code-review/SKILL.md` the SMART ROUTING section opens at line 49 and the first executable step block opens at line 67; the report's 364-line/50% measurement is consistent with the section boundaries I read. The opening sentence of `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:15` reads verbatim: "`quality` is the author-side quality gate MODE child of the `sk-code` family. It runs after the acting agent applying `workflow-implement.md` changes the code and before the surface's verification workflow or done-claim." The hub's own opening is a four-metaphor sentence: "One skill, two axes, one shared surface-detection router, and one advisor identity." (`SKILL.md:15`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:15] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:15]

**ROUTER.md §2 and §9 have drifted in both directions, not one.** The report's claim that §2 lists TESTING (`ROUTER.md:57`) and LANGUAGE_STANDARDS (`ROUTER.md:60`) with "no §9 key" is confirmed: §9 `INTENT_SIGNALS` runs `IMPLEMENTATION, CODE_QUALITY, DEBUGGING, VERIFICATION, HOOKS, CONFIG, JAVASCRIPT, TYPESCRIPT, PYTHON, SHELL, RUST, CI_WORKFLOW` (`ROUTER.md:241-252`). The report missed the converse: five §9 intents — JAVASCRIPT, TYPESCRIPT, PYTHON, SHELL, RUST — have no §2 prose row at all, so the "byte-for-byte source" claim at `ROUTER.md:223` holds for neither direction. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md:241]

**sk-code restates stage-one mode selection in four live places plus one generated artifact.** The registry is named the source of truth at `SKILL.md:54`; the same selection is re-expressed as Python `route()` at `SKILL.md:76-134`; as weighted classes in `hub-router.json:24-39`; as a 40-line prompt-keyword row in `ROUTER.md:252` (CI_WORKFLOW); and as the compiled projection `.skilled/bin/compiled-route.cjs` invoked at `SKILL.md:56-60`. `mode-registry.json` itself carries only 4 modes, with 83 aliases across them (13 quality, 10 review, 5 skilled, 55 ci). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:54] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:21]

**Stage-two leaf choice has no runtime script, so the leaf map is model-only.** `compiled-route.cjs` emits packets (`hub-router.json:24-39` `resources: ["<packet>/SKILL.md"]`), and `leaf-manifest.json` is a generated, checked artifact with no router consumer — its readers are tests and the compiler (`compiled-route-admission.cjs`, `parent-skill-check-leaf-manifest.test.cjs`). So D4 (which leaf files) is decided by prose and by each packet's own machine block, never by a resolver. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:24] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/leaf-manifest.json:1]

**The CI vocabulary is copied five times with three different sizes.** `hub-router.json:76-78` `code-ci-aliases` (55 keywords), `ROUTER.md:252` CI_WORKFLOW (61 keywords), `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:62` (12 keywords), `mode-registry.json` `sk-code-ci.aliases` (55), plus the packet's `RESOURCE_MAP` at `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:65`. The hub-router class and the registry alias list happen to agree today; the ROUTER.md row and the packet row do not, and the packet's own header admits the divergence is deliberate ("Every keyword is multi-word, so a bare 'workflow' never scores this surface", `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:56`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:76] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:62]

**The report's own inventory numbers are off and must be corrected before a plan quotes them.** It says `mode-registry.json`, "about 59 aliases"; the actual count is 83. It cites `hub-router.json:77` as a CI-vocabulary copy — line 77 is the `code-ci-aliases` keyword array, so the anchor is right but it is one class, not the class list. The direction of its conclusion survives; its quantities do not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:77]

**Three docs each claim a different routing authority.** `SKILL.md:54` says "`mode-registry.json` is the single source of truth"; `sk-code-review/SKILL.md:612` says "Keep Section 2 (`SMART ROUTING`) as the authoritative routing source"; `ROUTER.md:223` calls its §9 block "the byte-for-byte source a deterministic router parses". Only the third is measurably true — `parseRouter` reads the §9 block — so the other two are restatements that contradict the parser. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:612] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md:223]

**Two packets advertise routing the tooling does not read.** `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:30` carries a 15-term "Keyword triggers:" line and `sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:154-156` calls the deterministic router-replay "retired", while `sk-code-skilled/SKILL.md:178` documents that same replay as the live leg-1..4 guard. One of the two statements is stale; the guard is the one that runs. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-quality/SKILL.md:154] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/SKILL.md:178]

**Hub shape already diverges inside the same skill family.** sk-doc carries `leaf-aliases.json` (5 alias entries) and `leaf-scopes.json` in addition to `leaf-manifest.json`; sk-code carries only `leaf-manifest.json`. `leaf-aliases.json` is read by `router-replay-lib.cjs` and `parent-skill-check.cjs`, so the extra file changes which paths a guard can resolve — the hubs are not interchangeable inputs to the same checks. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/leaf-aliases.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/leaf-manifest.json:1]

**Nothing parses the declared source of truth.** A search of every `.cjs/.js/.ts/.py/.mjs` under `.skilled` and `.pi` for `Keyword triggers` returns zero code hits. The machine reader, `router-replay-lib.cjs`, resolves a hub's modes from `hub-router.json` and its leaves from `ROUTER.md`; the `Keyword triggers:` line is prose only. So sk-doc's "source of truth" is a convention enforced by review, not by a check. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/router-replay-lib.cjs:1]

**Readability: the routing definition is a 107-word run-on, and the trigger lines are ungrouped term dumps.** `sk-doc/SKILL.md:53` reads verbatim: "Routing is **registry-driven at runtime and packet-authored at source** in two stages. Stage 1 (hub → mode): each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections that the hub reads without re-deriving mappings during a request. The advisor routes any documentation/authoring query to the single identity `sk-doc`; the hub then picks the packet. Stage 2 (mode → leaves): the root `ROUTER.md` maps the request's authoring intent to the exact packet-local leaf resources that mode loads. The two layers stay separate: the hub never emits leaf paths, and the surface router never re-decides the mode." The frontmatter packet's trigger line (`sk-create-frontmatter/SKILL.md:36`) is 28 terms with no grouping, mixing field names, error symptoms and version formats. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-frontmatter/SKILL.md:36]

**sk-doc forbids the hub-level move the report proposes to test, by name and mechanism.** `SKILL.md:65` states the machine block "must not move into `SKILL.md` (the replay would treat it as the hub's own router and lose the mode projection) or into `hub-router.json` (schema handoff-ambiguity rule)". That is a hub-level constraint, not a packet-level one: no document forbids moving a packet's own block inside its own `SKILL.md`, which is where the block already lives. The report's plan is safe at packet level and blocked at hub level, and the two cases were conflated. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:65]

**Stage two is hub-owned in sk-doc and packet-owned in sk-code, on the same decision.** Only 5 of 14 sk-doc packets carry a `RESOURCE_MAP` machine block (`sk-create-benchmark:115`, `sk-create-frontmatter:80`, `sk-create-repo-rule:89`, `sk-create-skill:106`, `sk-create-with-human-voice:89`); the other 9 have no router block and depend entirely on `ROUTER.md` §3, which names every packet's leaves packet-qualified. sk-code does the reverse: all four packets carry blocks and the hub block duplicates them. Both shapes pass the same checks today, which matters for the verdict — one hub already demonstrates that per-mode blocks are optional. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/ROUTER.md:145] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-readme/SKILL.md:42]

**The "synchronized projection" claim is false today.** Comparing the 173 backticked terms across the 14 packets' `Keyword triggers:` lines with the union of `hub-router.json` vocabulary keywords finds 17 terms absent from the projection. `sk-create-diff` is the worst: 5 of its 7 triggers — `document before/after review`, `before/after document diff`, `review document edits`, `docx diff`, `pdf diff` — exist nowhere in `hub-router.json`. Every `/create:*` and `/doc:quality` slash form is also absent (for example `/create:readme`, `/create:skill-parent`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-diff/SKILL.md:30] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:1]

**The JSON cost grows with the mode count, and so does the drift surface.** sk-doc spends 605 lines of `mode-registry.json` and 477 of `hub-router.json` for 15 modes and 152 aliases — 40 registry lines per mode; sk-code spends 130 and 83 for 4 modes and 83 aliases — 33 lines per mode. The per-mode cost is roughly constant, so the alias drift in finding 3 is a function of mode count, not of the hub. A shape that keeps one JSON per hub must budget for that growth or generate it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/mode-registry.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:1]

**Two hubs assign opposite authorities to the same stage-one vocabulary.** sk-doc says "each nested packet's single `Keyword triggers:` line is the source of truth for its routing vocabulary; `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` are synchronized projections" (`sk-doc/SKILL.md:53`); sk-code says "`mode-registry.json` is the single source of truth" (`sk-code/SKILL.md:54`). Whichever wins, one hub's model is wrong today. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md:54]

**`workflowMode` means a different thing in system-deep-loop than in the other three hubs.** sk-code keys it by packet (`sk-code-review`, `SKILL.md:69`), sk-doc by packet (`SKILL.md:68`), sk-design by packet (`SKILL.md:80`); system-deep-loop keys it by loop (`research`, `review`, `ai-council`, `SKILL.md:59`) while its `hub-router.json` resources point at `deep-research/SKILL.md`. So the canonical `(workflowMode, leafResourceId)` pair has per-hub key semantics, and any cross-hub resolver has to special-case this hub. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:59] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/hub-router.json:24]

**Correction to iteration 2's cost estimate: growth is linear, the per-mode constant is not.** Registry lines per mode are sk-code 32.5, system-deep-loop 34.7, sk-doc 40.3, sk-design 51.5. The linear-in-mode-count claim holds; "roughly constant per mode" does not, because alias and `toolSurface` blocks vary by hub — so a generator must be parameterised per hub, not templated globally. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/mode-registry.json:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/mode-registry.json:1]

**Hub-level only: no document extends the forbid to a packet's own `SKILL.md`.** Every copy of the rule names "the machine block" moving into *the hub's* `SKILL.md` or into `hub-router.json`. Since a packet's machine block already lives in the packet's own `SKILL.md`, moving it within that file is outside the rule's wording. The advisor report conflated the two cases; the texts do not. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:50]

**Readability: a hard invariant sits inside the routing section of a 170-line hub.** `system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:54-58` carries a 96-word note explaining that the hub's `allowed-tools` grant must equal the union of every mode's `toolSurface.allowed` or `parent-skill-check.cjs` check 3j fails — a build constraint, not a routing rule, placed between the routing model and the discriminator. sk-design's `SKILL.md:61` opens a paragraph with the fragment "Four modes." after the table has already said so. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/SKILL.md:54] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/SKILL.md:61]

**sk-design restates the mode list a fourth time inside the hub.** `SKILL.md:54-60` is a four-column mode table (mode, command, owns, reach by asking), while the same list is the registry `modes[]`, the `hub-router.json` `routerSignals` keys and `tieBreak`, and the `ROUTER.md` intent model. The table is the copy most likely to drift, because nothing parses it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/SKILL.md:54]

**The no-match outcome has three names and no shared enum.** system-deep-loop writes "no keyword match → hub `defer`" (`SKILL.md:48`) and encodes `outcomes.defer` in `hub-router.json:11`; sk-code returns `load_level: "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK"` from its `route()` (`SKILL.md:110`); sk-doc writes "hub UNKNOWN fallback" (`ROUTER.md:405`) and sk-design "the hub's UNKNOWN fallback" (`SKILL.md:76`). A consumer that joins hub decisions cannot key on one value. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/hub-router.json:11] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/SKILL.md:71]

**The rule that blocks the hub-level move is copied in four hubs, and one copy has drifted.** sk-doc `SKILL.md:65`, system-deep-loop `SKILL.md:50` and cli-external-orchestration `SKILL.md:78` carry the sentence verbatim, including "(schema handoff-ambiguity rule)"; sk-design `SKILL.md:74` paraphrases it as "nor into `hub-router.json`, which is a different schema". The rule is the single most load-bearing constraint on the restructuring question, and its justification is now paraphrased in one of the four places that state it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:65] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-design/SKILL.md:74]

**The staleness claim does not reproduce.** `compiled-route-guard.cjs` reports all seven hubs `fresh` today, system-deep-loop included (`{"hubId":"system-deep-loop","ok":true,"reason":"fresh"}`), and the guard iterates the full hub list, not just sk-code. The report's note that "system-deep-loop reports a stale compiled manifest today" is stale itself, and the guard's coverage means any hub `SKILL.md` edit forces a re-mint while a packet edit does not. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/compiled-route-guard.cjs:168]

**`check-rule-copies.js` pins prose inside `sk-code-review/SKILL.md`.** Its `EXTENSION_FLOORS` block reads that file (`:169-170`) and the script's header says it exists "so no repository extension can reword or drop a floor unseen" (`:18`). A readability pass over review must leave those lines byte-identical or change the pin in the same commit. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/scripts/check-rule-copies.js:169]

**`package_skill.py` pins the section name and three marker words.** It requires an H2 named `SMART ROUTING` (`:69`, accepted variants `:79-80`), requires `discover_markdown_resources`, `_guard_in_skill` and `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` inside that section (`:182-184`), and validates it at `:769`. A shrunk 8-to-12-line §2 survives only if those three markers stay inside §2, which is compatible with the report's plan but rules out deleting the section. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/package_skill.py:182]

**A packet-root `ROUTER.md` is invisible to the replay, exactly as the report claimed — the anchor is the pointer regex.** `findReferencedRouterDoc` only accepts `references/[...].md` (`router-replay-lib.cjs:374`) or the convention path `references/smart-routing.md` (`:384`); a `ROUTER.md` at a packet root matches neither. Any per-mode router file is therefore unparseable by the component that verifies stage two. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/router-replay-lib.cjs:374]

**JSON-only for hubs fails a frozen contract code, not a style rule.** `root-router-contract.cjs` freezes `RRC-001 MISSING_ROOT_ROUTER`, `RRC-005 STAGE1_NONEMPTY` and `RRC-009 MISSING_PROSE_SECTION` (`:127-135`), and check 12a runs that library against every hub (`parent-skill-check.cjs:1787-1830`). Deleting a hub `ROUTER.md` therefore fails 12a with `RRC-001`; a stage1-only hub must also ship empty maps (`RRC-005`). JSON-only at hub level needs a contract revision, and the report's "RRC-001 if ROUTER.md goes away" is exactly right. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/scripts/lib/root-router-contract.cjs:127] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/parent-skill-check.cjs:1787]

**Leg 2 fails closed on a stage1-only hub, reproducing the report's finding.** `legSurfaceMap` pushes a problem when `SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES` is empty — "so the parent-tier check would be vacuous" (`verify-router-sync.cjs:198-200`) — and separately requires each surface `resourceMap` to be non-empty. A hub that legitimately delegates stage two to JSON breaks this leg even though the canon blesses `router_state: stage1-only`. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/verify-router-sync.cjs:198]

**Moving a packet's machine block anywhere inside the same `SKILL.md` is safe for `parseRouter`.** `parseRouter` extracts `INTENT_SIGNALS`/`RESOURCE_MAP` from the whole `SKILL.md` text (`router-replay-lib.cjs:397-403`) with no section or order constraint, so an appendix at the end of the file parses identically. The report's "may not be free" risk is resolvable without a tooling change at packet level. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/router-replay-lib.cjs:397]

**The compiler hashes the hub `SKILL.md` — and reads it from the `.opencode` mirror, not from `.skilled`.** `build-artifacts.cjs:44-58` sets `SKILL_ROOT = <repo>/.opencode/skills/sk-code` and hashes `SKILL.md`, `hub-router.json`, `mode-registry.json`. Packet `SKILL.md` files are not in the hash. Today `.skilled/skills/<hub>` and `.opencode/skills/<hub>` are separate real directories with identical bytes for all four hubs (sha256 match, checked), so any restructuring must be written to both or the compiled route compiles the old bytes. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/lib/compiled-routing/009-parent-hub-rollout/001-sk-code/harness/build-artifacts.cjs:44]

**The reach diagnostic consumes the document that JSON-only would delete.** `doctor-router-reach.yaml:64-65` takes stage-one vocabulary from `.skilled/skills/*/graph-metadata.json` and stage-two vocabulary from `.skilled/skills/*/ROUTER.md`, so removing a hub `ROUTER.md` removes that hub's stage-two reach input; the canon template additionally states the router is "first-class at the hub root as `ROUTER.md`, never at a nested path" (`parent-skill-root-router-template.md:20`), which forecloses per-mode routers by authoring rule as well as by parser. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-router-reach.yaml:65] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/assets/parent-skill/parent-skill-root-router-template.md:20]

**The router-sync guard covers sk-code only.** `verify-router-sync.cjs`'s every leg is keyed to the `SKCODE` constant (`SKCODE` root, `SURFACES = ['sk-code-ci','sk-code-skilled']`, `hubPacketDirs()` under `SKCODE`), and `readSkillRouter` reads `<packet>/SKILL.md` (`:47`). sk-doc's 14 packets, sk-design's 4 and system-deep-loop's 3 are outside the guard, which is why sk-doc's 9 router-less packets pass unnoticed. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/verify-router-sync.cjs:47]

**Plan, phase 0 — capture the baseline before any edit.** Record the current output of `compiled-route-guard.cjs --json` (7/7 fresh today), `verify-router-sync.cjs` (sk-code legs 1a-4), `parent-skill-check.cjs`, `check-rule-copies.js` and `package_skill.py --strict`. Without the baseline, a later "no regressions" claim cannot distinguish a pre-existing warning from a new one. Risk: none (read-only). Rollback: not applicable. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/compiled-route-guard.cjs:168]

**Plan, phase 1 — arrest drift inside JSON and inside §2/§9, before any restructuring.** Merge the CI vocabulary to one source (`hub-router.json` `code-ci-aliases`) and delete the three redundant copies at `ROUTER.md:252`, `sk-code-ci/SKILL.md:62` and the packet's prose; then make `ROUTER.md` §2 and §9 agree in both directions (add TESTING and LANGUAGE_STANDARDS to §9, or delete the five language intents from §9 and keep the language axis in `sk-code-skilled`). Risk: low — no contract file changes; `3d-alias` and `5k` catch duplicates and class mismatches. Rollback: revert the two JSON/MD files per hub, no re-mint needed because hub `SKILL.md` is untouched. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:76] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md:241]

**Plan, phase 2 — shrink mode-packet §2 in ascending blast order, never touching pinned lines.** Order: `sk-code-quality` (349), `sk-code-ci` (111), `sk-code-skilled` (226), `sk-code-review` (730) last. Each keeps an 8-to-12-line §2 that contains `discover_markdown_resources`, `_guard_in_skill` and `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` (the `package_skill.py:182-184` contract) and moves the Python block to a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` appendix, or deletes it where the hub names the leaves. Review's `EXTENSION_FLOORS` block (`check-rule-copies.js:169`) stays byte-identical. Risk: medium — leg 1b/3 read packet routers, so a deletion must land in the same change as the hub map that replaces it. Rollback: `git revert` per packet; no re-mint (packets are not hashed). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/scripts/package_skill.py:184] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/scripts/check-rule-copies.js:169]

**Plan, phase 3 — settle the sk-doc authority question with a generator, not a decision.** Either generate `hub-router.json` `vocabularyClasses` from the 14 packets' `Keyword triggers:` lines (adding a parser is the only way the declared source of truth becomes true), or declare `mode-registry.json` authoritative and delete the "source of truth" claim plus fix the 17 missing terms. The generator path is preferred because it makes `sk-doc/SKILL.md:53` true and removes 152 hand-maintained aliases. Risk: high — alias churn changes live routing; `3d-alias` and the router-reach allowlist are the safety net. Rollback: revert JSON and packet lines together; a partial revert leaves aliases duplicated and `3d-alias` fails loudly. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/SKILL.md:53]

**Plan, phase 4 — hub `SKILL.md` last, because it is the only edit that needs a re-mint and a mirror sync.** Replace each hub's `route()` pseudocode with a five-line statement plus a pointer to `compiled-route.cjs`, keep the hub-level "must not move" rationale in one place and link the other three hubs to it. Every hub `SKILL.md` edit requires the `.opencode` mirror to carry the same bytes (`build-artifacts.cjs:44-58` reads `.opencode`) and then a re-mint with `compiled-route-sync.cjs`; the guard is the only signal that this happened. Risk: high — a missed re-mint silently drops the hub to legacy routing, and the mirror-sync step's owner is UNKNOWN in this lineage. Rollback: `compiled-route-sync.cjs --revert <rollback-root>` restores the serving set, then revert the doc. [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/lib/compiled-routing/009-parent-hub-rollout/001-sk-code/harness/build-artifacts.cjs:44] [SOURCE: .skilled/bin/compiled-route-sync.cjs:1100]

**Plan, phase 5 — prose pass, then a deferred contract phase.** Apply the six clarity rules from the report plus "instructions before apparatus", re-run the baseline set plus `verify-doc-claims.cjs`, and defer any JSON-only ambition to a spec-level change that revises `RRC-001`/`RRC-009`, the reach glob and leg 2 together. Changing the contract is a different scope from changing the docs; conflating them is how a doc pass turns into an unguarded routing change. Risk: low for the prose pass, high for the contract phase, which should not start in the same packet. Rollback: prose is revert-only; the contract phase needs its own packet and its own rollback story.
